paper.title_en: Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
paper.abstract_en: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.
